solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Erica, over 50, in good shape

indicators.note: the plant is spread over the numeral, covering it, so the fifty sits inside it

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, so it gives heath
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A woman called Erica, past fifty, is still fit and well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erica' looks like a woman's name but is the plant genus of heaths; 'over' puts the plant around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good shape is a state of physical wellbeing, which is what the word names.

clue.text: Girl's toe squashed with this?

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl

indicators.note: something squashed is crushed out of shape, so the letters of toe are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl's toe gets crushed, perhaps by this very thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal adverb means to this or concerning this document, as in the documents attached hereto.

clue.text: A knight looks down on posh girl bearing around hot pasta

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit above, looking down on, the next
the manner comes around beside the abbreviation for heat, following it

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
gel is a plummy pronunciation of girl
H is the abbreviation for hot on a tap
air is a person's bearing or manner

explanation.surface: A knight looks down his nose at an upper-class girl wearing her hair up near something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'looks down on' places A and N above GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel hair is a very fine variety of spaghetti.

clue.text: American expression of approval of contact about award

indicators.note: about means around, so the contact goes round the award

parts.note: touch means contact, as in keep in touch
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An American gives an enthusiastic thumbs-up when someone gets in touch about a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Too much is dated American slang for excellent or wonderful, a cry of approval.

clue.text: Mean to live for a drink

indicators.note: for says one thing stands in place of another: to live takes the place of the a

parts.note: the mean of a set of numbers is its average
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone is told that getting by on little means they live for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals substitution: BE replaces the first A of AVERAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pitcher contributing to new error

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher's throw adds to the latest fielding mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug, and an ewer is a wide-mouthed water jug.

clue.text: Hide jealousy, ignoring unknown staff getting backing

indicators.note: ignoring the unknown means leaving that letter out

parts.note: envy is jealousy of what another has
Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: getting backing means turning back, so the word for staff is read backwards

parts.note: a pole is a staff or rod

explanation.surface: Someone conceals resentment, overlooking an unnamed employee who wins support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a pole; 'getting backing' turns POLE to ELOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop something is to wrap and cover it completely, hiding it from view.

clue.text: A priest on stage

explanation.surface: A clergyman appears in a theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: The apron is the part of a theatre stage that projects in front of the curtain.

clue.text: Work out duty bearing on being brought up

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the duty holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: excise is a duty levied on goods

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone works out how much tax is due on their upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like an instruction to solve but is the definition; 'being brought up' reads the short word upwards to ER, and 'bearing' carries it inside the duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out is to do physical training, which is exercise.

clue.text: Ignore broadcast in this area

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of the word ignore are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A local notice telling people to disregard a transmission in their district.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is a district or zone, the same idea as an area.

clue.text: Unreasonable for each to introduce part of chapter

indicators.note: to introduce means to come first, ahead of what follows

parts.note: per means for each, as in a pound per head
a Bible chapter is divided into numbered verses

explanation.surface: It seems unreasonable to make every person bring in a section of a chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse behaviour is contrary and wilfully unreasonable.

clue.text: The French revolutionary seduced by flawed dictum related to fundamental code

indicators.note: being seduced by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece goes inside the other
a flawed thing is broken, so the letters of dictum are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the French article is read backwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary is led astray by a faulty maxim about basic laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives AL; 'flawed' gives TMUDIC; 'seduced by' takes AL in just after the T. The Talmud is the codified body of Jewish law.
explanation.definitionFit: The Talmud is the body of Jewish law and commentary, a fundamental code, so the adjective relates to it.

clue.text: Inuits building at the original position

indicators.note: building implies constructing something new from material, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Inuit people constructing something where it first stood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original place, as archaeologists use it of undisturbed finds.

clue.text: Where to go with one's 15,150 in centre of Nice

parts.note: CL is the Roman numeral for 150

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here those of Nice

explanation.surface: Puzzling cross-reference: where to take your aches and pains in the middle of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across is ACHES AND PAINS. The comma joins the cross-reference 15 to the number 150.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical centre where ailing people go for treatment.

clue.text: Architect Jones pocketing penny for product of woad

indicators.note: pocketing means taking into a pocket, so the name holds the coin inside

parts.note: Inigo Jones was the seventeenth-century English architect of the Banqueting House
d is the abbreviation for an old British penny, from denarius

explanation.surface: An architect pockets a coin while painting with woad dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Woad is a plant yielding a blue dye; that dye is a deep blue colour of the same name.

clue.text: A visit to no.13 might be necessary after chewing Danish canapes

definitions.text: A visit to no.13 might be necessary

indicators.note: food that has been chewed is broken up, so the letters of the two words are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Eating rich Danish canapes might land you at the doctor's.
explanation.walkthrough: No.13 is the answer to 13 across, CLINIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor bodily complaints are the sort of thing that sends someone to a clinic.

clue.text: To start this month I punish students

parts.note: inst., for instant, is old business shorthand for this month
at Oxford and Cambridge students are gated, confined to college, as punishment

explanation.surface: A teacher announces that from this month on they will discipline pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: To gate a student, at British universities and boarding schools, is to keep them confined to college.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it going or bring it about.

clue.text: TV programme finding gold in country

indicators.note: a country finding gold has it within its borders, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Panama is a Central American country
or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: A television show discovers bullion in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is the long-running BBC current-affairs programme; 'gold' is the heraldic tincture, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Panorama is a well-known British television current-affairs series.

clue.text: Shiniest arrow deployed as being fit to fly

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gleaming arrow is shot, as though ready to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is the aviation word for an aircraft's fitness to fly safely.

clue.text: Blue, having died on site

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, coming first

parts.note: ob., for obiit, means died on gravestones
a scene is the site of an event, as the scene of the crime

explanation.surface: Feeling sad after a death at the location.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are indecent, which is the same as obscene.

clue.text: It's a kind of complex to choose God

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that selecting a deity is a psychological problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is Jung's term for a daughter's attachment to her father.

clue.text: Brownish odd fruit not right (twice)

indicators.note: not right means the letter standing for right is left out of the word for odd

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

indicators.note: twice says the same loss of the right letter happens again, to the fruit

parts.note: a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: A strange piece of fruit that has gone off is turning brown.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for right; both Rs removed from RUM BERRY leave the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a brown earth pigment, so the adjective means of an umber shade, brownish.

clue.text: No opening for escape route to get past old man-eater

indicators.note: the shortened word gets past, i.e. comes after, the abbreviation
with no opening the word loses its first letter

parts.note: an egress is a way out

explanation.surface: With no way out, someone must slip past an old cannibal.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ogre in fairy tales eats people, a literal man-eater.

clue.text: Miserable person's told gag

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a wretch is an unhappy or pitiable person

explanation.surface: An unhappy man is told a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a joke; here it means to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to make the involuntary motion of vomiting.

clue.text: Absurdity is only about doctrine

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
c, for circa, means about
an ism is any doctrine or creed

explanation.surface: A claim that the only absurdity concerns doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a blunder or impropriety, an incongruity that makes something absurd.

clue.text: French brute breathed oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A savage Frenchman breathes in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: Bête is the French word for beast, used in English in bête noire.

clue.text: Soldier was first to embrace queen with horny growth

parts.note: a soldier ant is a caste of ant

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside one's arms, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to have led is to have been first or in front
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A soldier, leading the way, hugs the queen and sprouts horns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is the ant, a crossword staple; 'to embrace' puts ER inside LED.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag with antlers has bony horn-like outgrowths on its head.

clue.text: Adult arousal unsatisfied, as resting

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
a tease rouses desire without satisfying it

explanation.surface: A frustrated grown-up is lying back, relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers standing at ease are in a relaxed resting position.

clue.text: A character always has to be high-flier

parts.note: chi is a Greek character, or letter
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Someone with good character who is always aiming high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter of the Greek alphabet, not a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-flier is a person who succeeds and accomplishes a great deal.

clue.text: Peter Tchaikovsky's cleared out as a condition of 18

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, hence a peterman, a safecracker

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its insides emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: The composer's belongings have been emptied out, all checked for being fit to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is AIRWORTHINESS. 'Peter' looks like the composer's first name but is slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is airworthy only when it is free from danger, so freedom from danger is a condition of it.
